 16284                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 16285                                  ;**	DPB - Drive Parameter Block
 16286                                  
 16287                                  ; 25/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0 (MSDOS 6.0, DPB.INC, 1991)
 16288                                  
 16289                                  ;	BUGBUG - this isn't authorative - it's my probably incomplete and
 16290                                  ;	possibly inaccurate deductions from code study... - jgl
 16291                                  ;
 16292                                  ;	The DPB is DOS's main structure for describing block devices.
 16293                                  ;	It contains info about the "Drive" intermingled with info about
 16294                                  ;	the FAT file system which is presumably on the drive.  I don't know
 16295                                  ;	how those fields are used if it's not the FAT file system - BUGBUG
 16296                                  ;
 16297                                  ;	The DPBs are statically allocated and chained off of DPBHead.
 16298                                  ;	Users scan this chain looking for a match on DPB_DRIVE.
 16299                                  ;	The DPBs are built at init time from info in the SYSDEV structure.
 16300                                  
 16301                                  ; 08/06/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0 (MSDOS 3.3, DPB.INC, 24/07/1987)
 16302                                  
 16303                                  ; 12/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 16304                                  
 16305                                  struc	DPB
 16306 00000000 ??                      .DRIVE:		resb 1		; Logical drive # assoc with DPB (A=0,B=1,...)
 16307 00000001 ??                      .UNIT:		resb 1		; Driver unit number of DPB
 16308 00000002 ????                    .SECTOR_SIZE:	resw 1		; Size of physical sector in bytes
 16309 00000004 ??                      .CLUSTER_MASK:	resb 1		; Sectors/cluster - 1
 16310 00000005 ??                      .CLUSTER_SHIFT:	resb 1		; Log2 of sectors/cluster
 16311 00000006 ????                    .FIRST_FAT:	resw 1		; Starting record of FATs
 16312 00000008 ??                      .FAT_COUNT:	resb 1		; Number of FATs for this drive
 16313 00000009 ????                    .ROOT_ENTRIES:	resw 1		; Number of directory entries
 16314 0000000B ????                    .FIRST_SECTOR:	resw 1		; First sector of first cluster
 16315 0000000D ????                    .MAX_CLUSTER:	resw 1		; Number of clusters on drive + 1
 16316                                  ;.FAT_SIZE:	resb 1  ; MSDOS 3.3
 16317 0000000F ????                    .FAT_SIZE:	resw 1		; Number of records occupied by FAT
 16318 00000011 ????                    .DIR_SECTOR:	resw 1		; Starting record of directory
 16319 00000013 ????????                .DRIVER_ADDR:	resd 1		; Pointer to driver
 16320 00000017 ??                      .MEDIA:		resb 1		; Media byte
 16321 00000018 ??                      .FIRST_ACCESS:	resb 1		; This is initialized to -1 to force a media
 16322                                  				; check the first time this DPB is used
 16323 00000019 ????????                .NEXT_DPB:	resd 1		; Pointer to next Drive parameter block
 16324 0000001D ????                    .NEXT_FREE:	resw 1		; Cluster # of last allocated cluster
 16325 0000001F ????                    .FREE_CNT:	resw 1		; Count of free clusters, -1 if unknown
 16326                                  .size:
 16327                                  endstruc

 16390                                  ;**	BIOS PARAMETER BLOCK DEFINITION
 16391                                  ;
 16392                                  ;	The BPB contains information about the disk structure.  It dates
 16393                                  ;	back to the earliest FAT systems and so FAT information is
 16394                                  ;	intermingled with physical driver information.
 16395                                  ;
 16396                                  ;	A boot sector contains a BPB for its device; for other disks
 16397                                  ;	the driver creates a BPB.  DOS keeps copies of some of this
 16398                                  ;	information in the DPB.
 16399                                  ;
 16400                                  ;	The BDS structure contains a BPB within it.
 16401                                  
 16402                                  struc A_BPB
 16403 00000000 ????                    .BPB_BYTESPERSECTOR:	resw	1
 16404 00000002 ??                      .BPB_SECTORSPERCLUSTER:	resb	1
 16405 00000003 ????                    .BPB_RESERVEDSECTORS:	resw	1
 16406 00000005 ??                      .BPB_NUMBEROFFATS:	resb	1
 16407 00000006 ????                    .BPB_ROOTENTRIES: 	resw	1
 16408 00000008 ????                    .BPB_TOTALSECTORS:	resw	1
 16409 0000000A ??                      .BPB_MEDIADESCRIPTOR:	resb	1
 16410 0000000B ????                    .BPB_SECTORSPERFAT:	resw	1
 16411 0000000D ????                    .BPB_SECTORSPERTRACK:	resw	1
 16412 0000000F ????                    .BPB_HEADS:		resw	1
 16413 00000011 ????                    .BPB_HIDDENSECTORS:	resw	1
 16414 00000013 ????                    			resw	1
 16415 00000015 ????                    .BPB_BIGTOTALSECTORS:	resw	1
 16416 00000017 ????                    			resw	1
 16417 00000019 ????????????            			resb	6	; NOTE:  many times these
 16418                                  ;					; 	 6 bytes are omitted
 16419                                  ;					;	 when BPB manipulations
 16420                                  ;					;	 are performed!
 16421                                  .size:
 16422                                  endstruc

 16681                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 16682                                  ; BIOSTRUC.INC (MSDOS 3.3 - 24/07/1987) 	
 16683                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 16684                                  					  ;;Rev 3.30 Modification
 16685                                  ; ROM BIOS CALL PACKET STRUCTURES					  
 16686                                  									  
 16687                                  ;*******************************					  
 16688                                  ;System Service call ( Int 15h )					  
 16689                                  ;*******************************					  
 16690                                  ;Function AH = 0C0h, Return system configuration			  
 16691                                  ;For PC and PCJR on return:						  
 16692                                  ;	(AH)	= 80h							  
 16693                                  ;	(CY)	= 1							  
 16694                                  ;For PCXT, PC PORTABLE and PCAT on return:				  
 16695                                  ;	(AH)	= 86h							  
 16696                                  ;	(CY)	= 1							  
 16697                                  ;For all others:							  
 16698                                  ;	(AH)	= 0							  
 16699                                  ;	(CY)	= 0							  
 16700                                  ;	(ES:BX) = pointer to system descriptor vector in ROS		  
 16701                                  ; System descriptor :							  
 16702                                  ;	DW	xxxx		length of descriptor in bytes,		  
 16703                                  ;				minimum length = 8			  
 16704                                  ;	DB	xx		model byte				  
 16705                                  ;				0FFh	= PC				  
 16706                                  ;				0FEh	= PC/XT, Portable		  
 16707                                  ;				0FDh	= PC/JR 			  
 16708                                  ;				0FCh	= PC/AT				  
 16709                                  ;				0F9h	= Convertable			  
 16710                                  ;				0F8h	= Model 80			  
 16711                                  ;				0E0 thru 0EFh = reserved		  
 16712                                  ;									  
 16713                                  ;	DB	xx		secondary model byte			  
 16714                                  ;				000h	= PC1				  
 16715                                  ;				000h	= PC/XT, Portable		  
 16716                                  ;				000h	= PC/JR 			  
 16717                                  ;				000h	= PC/AT 			  
 16718                                  ;				001h	= PC/AT Model 339		  
 16719                                  ;				003h	= PC/RT				  
 16720                                  ;				000h	= Convertable			  
 16721                                  ;									  
 16722                                  ;	DB	xx		bios revision level			  
 16723                                  ;				00 for first release, subsequent release  
 16724                                  ;				of code with same model byte and	  
 16725                                  ;				secondary model byte require revison level
 16726                                  ;				to increase by one.			  
 16727                                  ;									  
 16728                                  ;	DB	xx		feature information byte 1		  
 16729                                  ;				X0000000 = 1, bios use DMA channel 3	  
 16730                                  ;					 = 0, DMA channel 3 not used	  
 16731                                  ;									  
 16732                                  ;				0X000000 = 1, 2nd Interrupt chip present  
 16733                                  ;					 = 0, 2nd Interrupt chip not present
 16734                                  ;									  
 16735                                  ;				00X00000 = 1, Real Time Clock present	  
 16736                                  ;					 = 0, Real Time Clock not present 
 16737                                  ;									  
 16738                                  ;				000X0000 = 1, Keyboard escape sequence(INT 15h)
 16739                                  ;						called in keyboard interrupt
 16740                                  ;						(Int 09h).		  
 16741                                  ;					 = 0, Keyboard escape sequence not
 16742                                  ;						called. 		  
 16743                                  ;				0000XXXX reserved			  
 16744                                  ;									  
 16745                                  ;	DB	xx		feature information byte 2 - reserved	  
 16746                                  ;									  
 16747                                  ;	DB	xx		feature information byte 2 - reserved	  
 16748                                  ;									  
 16749                                  ;	DB	xx		feature information byte 2 - reserved	  
 16750                                  ;									  
 16751                                  ;	DB	xx		feature information byte 2 - reserved	  
 16752                                  ;									  
 16753                                  
 16754                                  ; 22/03/2019									  
 16755                                  struc ROMBIOS_DESC		; BIOS_SYSTEM_DESCRIPTOR						  
 16756 00000000 ????                    .bios_sd_leng:		resw 1

 16872                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 16873                                  ; CURDIR.INC (MSDOS 6.0 - 1991) 	
 16874                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 16875                                  ; 22/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 16876                                  
 16877                                  ;**	CDS - Current Directory Structure
 16878                                  ;
 16879                                  ; CDS items are used bu the internal routines to store cluster numbers and
 16880                                  ; network identifiers for each logical name.  The ID field is used dually,
 16881                                  ; both as net ID and for a cluster number for local devices. In the case
 16882                                  ; of local devices, the cluster number will be -1 if there is a potential
 16883                                  ; of the disk being changed or if the path must be recracked.
 16884                                  ;
 16885                                  ;	Some pathnames have special preambles, such as
 16886                                  ;
 16887                                  ;		\\machine\sharename\...
 16888                                  ;	For these pathnames we can't allow ".." processing to back us
 16889                                  ;	up into the special front part of the name.  The CURDIR_END field
 16890                                  ;	holds the address of the seperator character which marks
 16891                                  ;	the split between the special preamble and the regular
 16892                                  ;	path list; ".." processing isn't allowed to back us up past
 16893                                  ;	(i.e., before) CURDIR_END
 16894                                  ;	For the root, it points at the leading /. For net
 16895                                  ;	assignments it points at the end (nul) of the initial assignment:
 16896                                  ;	A:/	\\foo\bar	    \\foo\bar\blech\bozo
 16897                                  ;	  ^		 ^		     ^
 16898                                  
 16899                                  DIRSTRLEN	EQU	64+3		; Max length in bytes of directory strings
 16900                                  TEMPLEN 	EQU	DIRSTRLEN*2
 16901                                  
 16902                                  struc 		curdir_list
 16903                                  ; MSDOS 3.3
 16904 00000000 <res 43h>               .cdir_text	resb	DIRSTRLEN	; text of assignment and curdir
 16905 00000043 ????                    .cdir_flags	resw	1		; various flags
 16906 00000045 ????????                .cdir_devptr	resd	1		; local pointer to DPB or net device
 16907 00000049 ????????                .cdir_ID	resw	2		; cluster of current dir (net ID)
 16908 0000004D ????                    .cdir_usr_word	resw	1
 16909 0000004F ????                    .cdir_end	resw	1		; end of assignment
 16910                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
 16911 00000051 ??                      .cdir_type:	resb	1		; IFS drive (2=ifs, 4=netuse)
 16912 00000052 ????????                .cdir_ifd_hdr:	resd	1		; Ptr to File System Header
 16913 00000056 ????                    .cdir_fsda:	resb	2		; File System Dependent Data Area
 16914                                  .size:
 16915                                  endstruc

 16941                                  ;**	System File Table SuperStructure
 16942                                  ;
 16943                                  ;	The system file table entries are allocated in contiguous groups.
 16944                                  ;	There may be more than one such groups; the SF "superstructure"
 16945                                  ;	tracks the groups.
 16946                                  
 16947                                  struc	SF
 16948 00000000 ????????                .SFLink:	resd	1

 16951                                  .size:
 16952                                  endstruc
 16953                                  
 16954                                  ;**	System file table entry
 16955                                  ;
 16956                                  ;	These are the structures which are at SFTABLE in the SF structure.
 16957                                  
 16958                                  struc	SF_ENTRY
 16959 00000000 ????                    .sf_ref_count:	resw	1		; number of processes sharing entry
 16960                                  					;   if FCB then ref count
 16961 00000002 ????                    .sf_mode: 	resw	1		; mode of access or high bit on if FCB
 16962 00000004 ??                      .sf_attr: 	resb	1		; attribute of file
 16963 00000005 ????                    .sf_flags:	resw	1		;Bits 8-15
 16964                                  					; Bit 15 = 1 if remote file
 16965                                  					;	 = 0 if local file or device
 16966                                  					; Bit 14 = 1 if date/time is not to be
 16967                                  					;   set from clock at CLOSE.  Set by
 16968                                  					;   FILETIMES and FCB_CLOSE.  Reset by
 16969                                  					;   other reseters of the dirty bit
 16970                                  					;   (WRITE)
 16971                                  					; Bit 13 = Pipe bit (reserved)
 16972                                  					;
 16973                                  					; Bits 0-7 (old FCB_devid bits)
 16974                                  					; If remote file or local file, bit
 16975                                  					; 6=0 if dirty Device ID number, bits
 16976                                  					; 0-5 if local file.
 16977                                  					; bit 7=0 for local file, bit 7
 16978                                  					;      =1 for local I/O device
 16979                                  					; If local I/O device, bit 6=0 if EOF (input)
 16980                                  					;		Bit 5=1 if Raw mode
 16981                                  					;		Bit 0=1 if console input device
 16982                                  					;		Bit 1=1 if console output device
 16983                                  					;		Bit 2=1 if null device
 16984                                  					;		Bit 3=1 if clock device
 16985 00000007 ????????                .sf_devptr:	resd	1		; Points to DPB if local file, points
 16986                                  					; to device header if local device,
 16987                                  					; points to net device header if
 16988                                  					; remote

 17299                                  
 17300                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 17301                                  ; 21/10/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS - SYSINIT)
 17302                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 17303                                  
 17304                                  ;	MSStack.inc
 17305                                  ;
 17306                                  ;	Interrupt level 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7,(10, 11, 12, 14, 15 - AT level)
 17307                                  ;	should follow the standard Interrupt Sharing Scheme which has
 17308                                  ;	a standard header structure.
 17309                                  ;	Fyi, the following shows the relations between
 17310                                  ;	the interrupt vector and interrupt level.
 17311                                  ; VEC(Hex)    2  8  9  A  B  C	D  E  70  72  73  74  76  77
 17312                                  ; LVL(Deci)   9  0  1  2  3  4	5  6   8  10  11  12  14  15
 17313                                  ;	MSSTACK module modifies the following interrupt vectors
 17314                                  ;	to meet the standard Interrupt Sharing standard;
 17315                                  ;	  A, B, C, D, E, 72, 73, 74, 76, 77.
 17316                                  ;	Also, for interrupt level 7 and 15, the FirstFlag in a standard header
 17317                                  ;	should be initialized to indicat whether this interrupt handler is
 17318                                  ;	the first (= 80h) or not.  The FirstFlag entry of INT77h's
 17319                                  ;	program header is initialized in STKINIT.INC module.
 17320                                  ;	FirstFlag is only meaningful for interrupt level 7 and 15.
 17321                                  ;
 17322                                  
 17323                                  ;  User specifies the number of stack elements - default = 9
 17324                                  ;						 minimum = 8
 17325                                  ;						 maximum = 64
 17326                                  ;
 17327                                  ;  Intercepts Asynchronous Hardware Interrupts only
 17328                                  ;
 17329                                  ;  Picks a stack from pool of stacks and switches to it
 17330                                  ;
 17331                                  ;  Calls the previously saved interrupt vector after pushing flags
 17332                                  ;
 17333                                  ;  On return, returns the stack to the stack pool
 17334                                  ;
 17335                                  
 17336                                  ; This is a modification of STACKS:
 17337                                  ; 1. To fix a bug which was causing the program to take up too much space.
 17338                                  ; 2. To dispense stack space from hi-mem first rather than low-mem first.
 17339                                  ;    . Clobbers the stack that got too big instead of innocent stack
 17340                                  ;    . Allows system to work if the only stack that got too big was the most
 17341                                  ;      deeply nested one
 17342                                  ; 3. Disables NMI interrupts while setting the NMI vector.
 17343                                  ; 4. Does not intercept any interupts on a PCjr.
 17344                                  ; 5. Double checks that a nested interrupt didn't get the same stack.
 17345                                  ; 6. Intercepts Ints 70, 72-77 for PC-ATs and other future products
 17346                                  
 17347                                  		;EVEN
 17348                                  ;align 2
 17349                                  		; 21/10/2022
 17350                                  
 17351 00000000 0000                    		dw	0	; spare field but leave these in order
 17352 00000002 0000                    stackcount:	dw	0
 17353 00000004 0000                    stackat: 	dw	0
 17354 00000006 0000                    stacksize:	dw	0
 17355 00000008 0000                    stacks:		dw	0
 17356 0000000A 0000                    		dw	0
 17357                                  
 17358 0000000C [0800]                  firstentry:	dw	stacks
 17359 0000000E [4800]                  lastentry:	dw	stacks+(defaultcount*entrysize)-entrysize
 17360 00000010 [4800]                  nextentry:	dw	stacks+(defaultcount*entrysize)-entrysize
 17361                                  
 17362                                  ;***********************************************************************
 17363                                  ; THESE ARE THE INDIVIDUAL INTERRUPT HANDLERS
 17364                                  
 17365                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 17366                                  
 17367 00000012 00000000                old02:	dd	0
 17368                                  
 17369                                  int02:
 17370                                  
 17371                                  ; *********************************************************************
 17372                                  ;
 17373                                  ; this is special support for the pc convertible / nmi handler
 17374                                  ;
 17375                                  ;	on the pc convertible, there is a situation where an nmi can be 
 17376                                  ;	caused by using the "out" instructions to certain ports. when this
 17377                                  ;	occurs, the pc convertible hardware *guarantees* that **nothing** 
 17378                                  ;	can stop the nmi or interfere with getting to the nmi handler. this
 17379                                  ;	includes other type of interrupts (hardware and software), and
 17380                                  ;	also includes other type of nmi's. when any nmi has occured,
 17381                                  ;	no other interrtupt (hardware, software or nmi) can occur until
 17382                                  ;	the software takes specific steps to allow further interrupting.
 17383                                  ;
 17384                                  ;	for pc convertible, the situation where the nmi is generated by the
 17385                                  ;	"out" to a control port requires "fixing-up" and re-attempting. in
 17386                                  ;	otherwords, it is actually a "restartable exception". in this
 17387                                  ;	case, the software handler must be able to get to the stack in
 17388                                  ;	order to figure out what instruction caused the problem, where
 17389                                  ;	it was "out"ing to and what value it was "out"ing.  therefore,
 17390                                  ;	we will not switch stacks in this situation. this situation is
 17391                                  ;	detected by interrogating port 62h, and checking for a bit value
 17392                                  ;	of 80h. if set, *****do not switch stacks*****.
 17393                                  ;
 17394                                  ; *********************************************************************
 17395                                  
 17396 00000016 50                      	push	ax
 17397 00000017 06                      	push	es
 17398 00000018 B800F0                  	mov	ax,0F000h
 17399 0000001B 8EC0                    	mov	es,ax
 17400                                  	; 02/11/2022
 17401 0000001D 26803EFEFFF9            	cmp	byte [es:0FFFEh],0F9h ; mdl_convert ; check if convertible
 17402 00000023 07                      	pop	es
 17403 00000024 750C                    	jne	short normal02
 17404                                  
 17405 00000026 E462                    	in	al,62h		; PC/XT PPI port C. Bits:
 17406                                  				; 0-3: values of DIP switches
 17407                                  				; 5: 1=Timer 2 channel out
 17408                                  				; 6: 1=I/O channel check
 17409                                  				; 7: 1=RAM parity check error occurred.
 17410 00000028 A880                    	test	al,80h
 17411 0000002A 7406                    	jz	short normal02
 17412                                  special02:
 17413 0000002C 58                      	pop	ax

 17649                                  
 17650                                  ; do interrupt stack switching. the fake return address holds
 17651                                  ; a pointer to the far-pointer of the actual interrupt
 17652                                  ; service routine
 17653                                  
 17654                                  ; 21/10/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 SYSINIT)
 17655                                  ; 21/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 17656                                  
 17657                                  ;allocbyte   equ 0
 17658                                  ;intlevel    equ 1
 17659                                  ;savedsp     equ 2
 17660                                  ;savedss     equ 4
 17661                                  ;newsp       equ 6
 17662                                  
 17663                                  ; 30/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.2 (Modified MSDOS 6.21 SYSINIT)
 17664                                  ; (MSDOS 6.21 IO.SYS, SYSINIT:0147h)
 17665                                  
 17666                                  do_int_stacks:
 17667 00000147 50                      	push	ax
 17668 00000148 55                      	push	bp
 17669 00000149 06                      	push	es
 17670 0000014A 2E8E06[0A00]            	mov	es,[cs:stacks+2]	; Get segment of stacks
 17671 0000014F 2E8B2E[1000]            	mov	bp,[cs:nextentry]	; get most likely candidate
 17672 00000154 B001                    	mov	al,allocated ; 1
 17673                                  	; 21/10/2022
 17674                                  	;xchg	[es:bp+allocbyte],al 
 17675                                  	; 11/12/2022
 17676 00000156 26864600                	xchg	[es:bp],al		; grab the entry
 17677 0000015A 3C00                    	cmp	al,free ; 0		; still avail?
 17678 0000015C 7551                    	jne	short notfree02
 17679                                  
 17680 0000015E 2E832E[1000]08          	sub	word [cs:nextentry],entrysize ; set for next interrupt
 17681                                  found02:
 17682 00000164 26896602                	mov	[es:bp+savedsp],sp	; save sp value
 17683 00000168 268C5604                	mov	[es:bp+savedss],ss	; save ss also
 17684                                  
 17685 0000016C 89E8                    	mov	ax,bp			; temp save of table offset
 17686                                  
 17687 0000016E 268B6E06                	mov	bp,[es:bp+newsp]	; get new SP value
 17688                                  	; 21/10/2022
 17689                                  	;mov	bp,[es:bp+6]
 17690                                  	; 11/12/2022
 17691                                  	;cmp	[es:bp+0],ax	
 17692 00000172 26394600                	cmp	[es:bp],ax		; check for offset into table
 17693 00000176 7544                    	jne	short foundbad02
 17694                                  
 17695                                  	; 02/07/2023 (MSDOS 6.21 SYSINIT code)
 17696 00000178 8CC0                    	mov	ax,es			; point ss,sp to the new stack
 17697 0000017A 8EC5                    	mov	es,bp
 17698 0000017C 89E5                    	mov	bp,sp
 17699 0000017E 8B6E06                  	mov	bp,[bp+6]
 17700 00000181 8ED0                    	mov	ss,ax
 17701 00000183 8CC4                    	mov	sp,es
 17702 00000185 8EC0                    	mov	es,ax
 17703 00000187 2E8B6E00                	mov	bp,[cs:bp]
 17704                                  
 17705                                  	; 21/10/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 SYSINIT code)
 17706                                  	;push    bp
 17707                                  	;mov     bp,sp
 17708                                  	;mov     ax,[bp+8]
 17709                                  	;pop     bp
 17710                                  	;push    es
 17711                                  	;pop     ss
 17712                                  	;mov     sp,bp
 17713                                  	;mov     bp,ax
 17714                                  	; 11/12/2022
 17715                                  	;;mov	bp,[cs:bp+0]	
 17716                                  	;mov	bp,[cs:bp]	
 17717                                  
 17718 0000018B 9C                      	pushf				; go execute the real interrupt handler
 17719                                  	; 11/12/2022
 17720 0000018C 2EFF5E00                	call	far [cs:bp]		; which will iret back to here
 17721                                  	; 21/10/2022
 17722                                  	;call	far [cs:bp+0]
 17723                                  
 17724 00000190 89E5                    	mov	bp,sp			; retrieve the table offset for us
 17725                                  	; 11/12/2022
 17726 00000192 268B6E00                	mov	bp,[es:bp]		; but leave it on the stack
 17727                                  	; 21/10/2022
 17728                                  	;mov	bp,[es:bp+0]
 17729 00000196 268E5604                	mov	ss,[es:bp+savedss]	; get old stack back
 17730 0000019A 268B6602                	mov	sp,[es:bp+savedsp]
 17731                                  
 17732                                  	; 11/12/2022
 17733                                  	;mov	byte [es:bp+allocbyte],free ; free the entry
 17734                                  	; 21/10/2022
 17735 0000019E 26C6460000              	mov	byte [es:bp],free ; 0
 17736 000001A3 2E892E[1000]            	mov	[cs:nextentry],bp	; setup to use next time
 17737                                  
 17738 000001A8 07                      	pop	es			; saved on entry
 17739 000001A9 5D                      	pop	bp			; saved on entry
 17740 000001AA 58                      	pop	ax			; saved on entry

 19467                                  ; we are going to open the command interpreter and size it as is done in
 19468                                  ; ldfil. the reason we must do this is that sysinit is in free memory. if
 19469                                  ; there is not enough room for the command interpreter,exec will probably
 19470                                  ; overlay our stack and code so when it returns with an error sysinit won't be
 19471                                  ; here to catch it. this code is not perfect (for instance .exe command
 19472                                  ; interpreters are possible) because it does its sizing based on the
 19473                                  ; assumption that the file being loaded is a .com file. it is close enough to
 19474                                  ; correctness to be usable.

 19842                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 19843                                  ; procedure : AllocFreeMem
 19844                                  ;
 19845                                  ; Allocate Max memory from DOS to find out where to load DOS.
 19846                                  ; DOS is at temporary location when this call is being made
 19847                                  ;
 19848                                  ; Inputs : None
 19849                                  ; Outputs: The biggest chunk of memory is allocated (all mem at init time)
 19850                                  ;	   [area] & [memhi] set to the para value of the start of the
 19851                                  ;	   free memory.
 19852                                  ;
 19853                                  ; Uses   : AX, BX

 20368                                  ; BUGBUG -- 5 Aug 92 -- chuckst -- Allocating space for DOS
 20369                                  ;	  using DOS itself causes an arena to be generated.
 20370                                  ;	  Unfortunately, certain programs (like PROTMAN$)
 20371                                  ;	  assume that the device drivers are loaded into
 20372                                  ;	  the first arena. For this reason, MagicDrv's
 20373                                  ;	  main device driver header arena is manually
 20374                                  ;	  truncated from the arena chain, and the space
 20375                                  ;	  for DOS is allocated using the following
 20376                                  ;	  simple code, which also assumes that the

 20616                                  ;
 20617                                  ; following piece of code will be moved into a para boundary. And the para
 20618                                  ; address posted in seg of int 19h vector. Offset of int 19h will point to
 20619                                  ; VDint19. This is to protect HMA from apps which use VDISK header method
 20620                                  ; to determine free extended memory.
 20621                                  ;
 20622                                  ; For more details read "power programming" column by Ray Duncan in the
 20623                                  ; May 30 1989 issue of PC Magazine (pp 377-388) [USING EXTENDED MEMORY,PART 1]

 20629

 20632 00000AC6 0000                    	dw	0		; strategy routine offset
 20633 00000AC8 0000                    	dw	0		; interrupt routine offset
 20634 00000ACA 01                      	db	1		; number of units
 20635                                  	;db	7 dup(0) 
 20636 00000ACB 00<rep 7h>              	times	7 db 0 		; reserved area

 20638 00000AD2 564449534B              	db	'VDISK'
 20639                                  
 20640                                  VLEN1	equ	($-VDiskSig1)
 20641

 20643                                  	;db	15 dup (0)	; pad

 20645 00000AEC 0000                    	dw	0		; bits 0-15 of free HMA
 20646 00000AEE 11                      	db	11h		; bits 16-23 of free HMA (1M + 64K)

 22158                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 22159                                  ; Do_Install_Exec
 22160                                  ;
 22161                                  ; This procedure is used to EXEC a program being loaded via the 
 22162                                  ; "install=" mechanism in config.sys. It does this by setting up
 22163                                  ; the parameters, and then jumping to sysinit_base, which has been
 22164                                  ; setup in low memory. When complete, sysinit_base will jump back
 22165                                  ; up to this procedure (if sysinit remains uncorrupted by the installed
 22166                                  ; program).
 22167                                  
 22168                                  ;SYSINIT:10CFh:
 22169                                  
 22170                                  do_install_exec:			; now,handles install= command.
 22171                                  
 22172 000010B3 56                      	push	si			; save si for config.sys again.
 22173                                  
 22174                                  ; we are going to call load/exec function.
 22175                                  ; set es:bx to the parameter block here;;;;;;;
 22176                                  ; set ds:dx to the asciiz string. remember that we already has 0
 22177                                  ; after the filename. so parameter starts after that. if next
 22178                                  ; character is a line feed (i.e. 10),then assume that the 0
 22179                                  ; we already encountered used to be a carrage return. in this
 22180                                  ; case,let's set the length to 0 which will be followed by
 22181                                  ; carridge return.
 22182                                  
 22183                                  ; es:si -> command line in config.sys. points to the first non blank
 22184                                  ;character after =.
 22185

 22187 000010B5 1E                      	push	ds
 22188 000010B6 07                      	pop	es
 22189 000010B7 1F                      	pop	ds			; es->sysinitseg,ds->confbot seg

 22332                                  ;
 22333                                  ;	ParaRound rounds a byte count up to a multiple of 16, then divides
 22334                                  ;	by 16 yielding a "length in paragraphs" value.
 22335                                  ;
 22336                                  ;	ENTRY	(ax) = byte length
 22337                                  ;	EXIT	(ax) = rounded up length in paragraphs
 22338                                  ;	USES	ax, flags
 22339                                  
 22340                                  ParaRound:

 22348                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 22349                                  ; sysinit_base module.
 22350                                  ;
 22351                                  ; This module is relocated by the routine EndFile to a location in low
 22352                                  ; memory. It is then called by SYSINIT to perform the EXEC of programs
 22353                                  ; that are being loaded by the "install=" command. After the EXEC call
 22354                                  ; completes, this module performs a checksum on the SYSINIT code (at the
 22355                                  ; top of memory) to be sure that the EXECed program did not damage it.
 22356                                  ; If it did, then this module will print an error message and stop the
 22357                                  ; system. Otherwise, it returns control to SYSINIT.
 22358                                  ;
 22359                                  ;in: after relocation,
 22360                                  ;    ax = 4b00h - load and execute the program dos function.
 22361                                  ;    ds = confbot. segment of config.sys file image
 22362                                  ;    es = sysinitseg. segment of sysinit module itself.
 22363                                  ;    ds:dx = pointer to asciiz string of the path,filename to be executed.
 22364                                  ;    es:bx = pointer to a parameter block for load.
 22365                                  ;    SI_end (byte) - offset value of end of sysinit module label
 22366                                  ;    bigsize (word) - # of word from confbot to SI_end.
 22367                                  ;    chksum (word) - sum of every byte from confbot to SI_end in a
 22368                                  ;			word boundary moduler form.
 22369                                  ;    sysinit_ptr (dword ptr) - return address to sysinit module.
 22370                                  ;
 22371                                  ;note: sysinit should save necessary registers and when the control is back
 22372                                  
 22373                                  	; 24/10/2022
 22374                                  	; (SYSINIT:115Ch for MSDOS 5.0 SYSINIT)
 22375                                  sysinit_base:				
 22376 0000113B 2E8C166200              	mov	[cs:sysinit_base_ss],ss	; save stack
 22377 00001140 2E89266400              	mov	[cs:sysinit_base_sp],sp	
 22378 00001145 CD21                    	int	21h			; load/exec dos call.
 22379 00001147 2E8E166200              	mov	ss,[cs:sysinit_base_ss]	; restore stack
 22380 0000114C 2E8B266400              	mov	sp,[cs:sysinit_base_sp]
 22381 00001151 1F                      	pop	ds			; restore confbot seg
 22382 00001152 07                      	pop	es			; restore sysinitseg
 22383 00001153 7216                    	jc	short sysinit_base_end	; load/exec function failed.
 22384                                  					; at this time,i don't have to worry about
 22385                                  					; that sysinit module has been broken or not.
 22386 00001155 E81800                  	call	sum_up			; otherwise,check if it is good.
 22387 00001158 263906[DA02]            	cmp	[es:checksum],ax
 22388 0000115D 740C                    	je	short sysinit_base_end
 22389                                  
 22390                                  ;	memory broken. show "memory allocation error" message and stall.
 22391                                  
 22392 0000115F B409                    	mov	ah,9
 22393 00001161 0E                      	push	cs
 22394 00001162 1F                      	pop	ds
 22395                                  	; 30/12/2022
 22396                                  	; (MSDOS 6.21 IO.SYS, SYSINIT:12B8h)
 22397                                  	;mov	dx,102
 22398 00001163 BA6600                  	mov	dx,mem_alloc_err_msgx-sysinit_base ; 65h (for MSDOS 5.0 SYSINIT)
 22399                                  					; 66h (for MSDOS 6.21 SYSINIT)
 22400 00001166 CD21                    	int	21h
 22401                                  		; DOS - PRINT STRING
 22402                                  		; DS:DX -> string terminated by "$"
 22403                                  
 22404                                  	; 30/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.2
 22405                                  stall:
 22406                                  	; 24/10/2022
 22407                                  _stall: 
 22408                                  	; 11/12/2022
 22409 00001168 F4                      	hlt 
 22410                                  	; 02/11/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS SYSINIT compatibility)
 22411                                  	;hlt				;use HLT to minimize energy consumption
 22412 00001169 EBFD                            jmp	short _stall

 22571                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 22572                                  ; procedure : GetBufferAddr
 22573                                  ;
 22574                                  ;	      Gets the buffer address either in HMA or in Lo Mem
 22575                                  ;

 22577                                  ; returns NZ if allocated in HMA

 22582 00001216 53                      	push	bx
 22583 00001217 52                      	push	dx

 22651                                  
 22652                                  ; ======================================================================
 22653                                  ; MSSTACK initialization routine - MSDOS 6.0 - SYSDINIT1.ASM - 1991
 22654                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 22655                                  ; 27/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 22656                                  
 22657                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 22658                                  ; ibmstack initialization routine.
 22659                                  ;
 22660                                  ;	to follow the standard interrupt sharing scheme, msstack.asm
 22661                                  ;	has been modified. this initialization routine also has to
 22662                                  ;	be modified because for the interrupt level 7 and 15, firstflag
 22663                                  ;	should be set to signal that this interrupt handler is the
 22664                                  ;	first handler hooked to this interrupt vector.
 22665                                  ;	we determine this by looking at the instruction pointed by
 22666                                  ;	this vector. if it is iret, then this handler should be the
 22667                                  ;	first one. in our case, only the interrupt vector 77h is the
 22668                                  ;	interrupt level 15. (we don't hook interrupt level 7.)
 22669                                  ;
 22670                                  ;	the followings are mainly due to m.r.t; ptm fix of p886 12/3/86
 22671                                  ;	some design changes are needed to the above interrupt sharing
 22672                                  ;	method. the above sharing scheme assumes that 1). interrupt
 22673                                  ;	sharing is never done on levels that have bios support. 2). "phantom"
 22674                                  ;	interrupts would only be generated on levels 7 and 15.
 22675                                  ;	these assumptions are not true any more. we have to use the firstflag
 22676                                  ;	for every level of interrupt. we will set the firstflag on the following
 22677                                  ;	conditions:
 22678                                  ;
 22679                                  ;	 a.	 if the cs portion of the vector is 0000, then "first"
 22680                                  ;	 b. else if cs:ip points to valid shared header, then not "first"
 22681                                  ;	 c. else if cs:ip points to an iret, then "first"
 22682                                  ;	 d. else if cs:ip points to dummy, then "first"
 22683                                  ;
 22684                                  ;	where dummy is - the cs portion must be f000, and the ip portion must
 22685                                  ;	be equal to the value at f000:ff01. this location is the initial value
 22686                                  ;	from vector_table for interrupt 7, one of the preserved addresses in all
 22687                                  ;	the bioses for all of the machines.
 22688                                  ;
 22689                                  ;	system design group requests bios to handle the phantom interrupts.
 22690                                  ;
 22691                                  ;	the "phantom" interrupt is an illegal interrupt such as an interrupt
 22692                                  ;	produced by the bogus adapter card even without interrupt request is
 22693                                  ;	set.  more specifically, 1). the 8259 has a feature when running in
 22694                                  ;	edge triggered mode to latch a pulse and present the interrupt when
 22695                                  ;	the processor indicates interrupt acknowledge (inta). the interrupt
 22696                                  ;	pulse was exist at the time of inta to get a "phantom" interrupt.
 22697                                  ;	2). or, this is caused by adapter cards placing a glitch on the
 22698                                  ;	interrupt line.
 22699                                  ;
 22700                                  ;	to handle those "phantom" interrupts, the main stack code will check
 22701                                  ;	the own firstflag, and if it is not "first" (which means the forward
 22702                                  ;	pointer points to the legal shared interrupt handler), then pass the
 22703                                  ;	control. if it is the first, then the following action should be
 22704                                  ;	taken. we don't have to implement stack logic in this case.
 22705                                  ;
 22706                                  ;	to implement this logic, we rather choose a simple method.
 22707                                  ;	if ont of the above "firstflag" conditions is met, we are not
 22708                                  ;	going to hook this interrupt vector. the reason is if the original
 22709                                  ;	vector points to "iret" and do nothing, we don't need
 22710                                  ;	to implement the stack logic for it. this will simplify implementation
 22711                                  ;	while maintaining compatibility with the old version of dos.
 22712                                  ;	this implies that in the main stack code, there might be a stack code
 22713                                  ;	that will never be used, a dead code.
 22714                                  ;
 22715                                  ;in - cs, ds -> sysinitseg, es -> relocated stack code & data.
 22716                                  
 22717                                  	; 25/10/2022 - Retro DOS 4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS, SYSINIT)
 22718                                  	; (SYSINIT:1287h)
 22719                                  
 22720                                  	; 14/12/2022

 23562                                  ; 25/10/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS, SYSINIT)
 23563                                  ; (SYSINIT:1610h)
 23564                                  
 23565                                  ; 13/04/2024 - Retro DOS v4.2 (Modified MSDOS 6.22 IO.SYS, SYSINIT)
 23566                                  ; (SYSINIT:1745h)
 23567                                  
 23568                                  new_init_loop:
 23569                                  
 23570                                  ;input: si=ofset into vector table of the particular int vector being adjusted
 23571                                  ;	bx=ds:offset of oldxx, where will be saved the pointer to original owner
 23572                                  ;	dx=ds:offset of intxx, the new interrupt handler
 23573                                  ;	di=offset value of int19old&aa variable in bios.
 23574                                  ;	es=zero, segid of vector table
 23575                                  ;	ds=relocated stack code segment
 23576                                  
 23577                                  ; 13/04/2024
 23578                                  %if 0
 23579                                  	mov	ax,[es:si]		;remember offset in vector
 23580                                  	mov	[bx],ax			; to original owner in ds
 23581                                  	mov	ax,[es:si+2]		;remember segid in vector
 23582                                  	mov	[bx+2],ax		; to original owner in ds
 23583                                  
 23584                                  	push	ds
 23585                                  	;;mov	ax,Bios_Data ; 70h
 23586                                  	;mov	ax,KERNEL_SEGMENT ; 70h
 23587                                  	; 21/10/2022
 23588                                  	mov	ax,DOSBIODATASEG ; 0070h
 23589                                  	mov	ds,ax			;set int19oldxx value in bios for
 23590                                  	mov	ax,[es:si]		;int 19 handler
 23591                                  	mov	[di],ax
 23592                                  	mov	ax,[es:si+2]
 23593                                  	mov	[di+2],ax
 23594                                  	pop	ds
 23595                                  %else
 23596                                  	; 13/04/2024 - Retro DOS v4.2
 23597 00001455 1E                      	push	ds
 23598 00001456 268B4402                	mov	ax,[es:si+2]		;remember segid in vector
 23599 0000145A 894702                  	mov	[bx+2],ax		; to original owner in ds
 23600 0000145D 50                      	push	ax
 23601 0000145E 268B04                  	mov	ax,[es:si]		;remember offset in vector
 23602 00001461 8907                    	mov	[bx],ax			; to original owner in ds
 23603 00001463 50                      	push	ax
 23604 00001464 B87000                  	mov	ax,DOSBIODATASEG ; 0070h
 23605 00001467 8ED8                    	mov	ds,ax			;set int19oldxx value in bios for
 23606 00001469 58                      	pop	ax			;int 19 handler
 23607 0000146A 8905                    	mov	[di],ax
 23608 0000146C 58                      	pop	ax
 23609 0000146D 894502                  	mov	[di+2],ax
 23610 00001470 1F                      	pop	ds
 23611                                  %endif
 23612 00001471 268914                  	mov	[es:si],dx  	;set vector to point to new int handler
 23613 00001474 268C5C02                	mov	[es:si+2],ds
 23614 00001478 C3                      	retn

 23904                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 23905                                  ; << Control field definition  >>
 23906                                  ;
 23907                                  ;
 23908                                  ;CONTROL   LABEL   BYTE
 23909                                  ;	   DW	   MATCH_FLAGS	   ; CONTROLS TYPE MATCHED
 23910                                  ;				   ; 8000H=NUMERIC VALUE, (VALUE LIST WILL BE CHECKED)
 23911                                  ;				   ; 4000H=SIGNED NUMERIC VALUE (VALUE LIST WILL BE CHECKED)
 23912                                  ;				   ; 2000H=SIMPLE STRING(VALUE LIST WILL BE CHECKED)
 23913                                  ;				   ; 1000H=DATE STRING (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23914                                  ;				   ; 0800H=TIME STRING (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23915                                  ;				   ; 0400H=COMPLEX LIST (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23916                                  ;				   ; 0200H=FILE SPEC (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23917                                  ;				   ; 0100H=DRIVE ONLY (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23918                                  ;				   ; 0080H=QUOTED STRING (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23919                                  ;				   ; 0010H=IGNORE ":" AT END IN MATCH
 23920                                  ;				   ; 0002H=REPEATS ALLOWED
 23921                                  ;				   ; 0001H=OPTIONAL
 23922                                  ;	   DW	   FUNCTION_FLAGS
 23923                                  ;				   ; 0001H=CAP RESULT BY FILE TABLE
 23924                                  ;				   ; 0002H=CAP RESULT BY CHAR TABLE
 23925                                  ;				   ; 0010H=REMOVE ":" AT END
 23926                                  ; (tm10)			   ; 0020H=colon is not necessary for switch
 23927                                  ;	   DW	   RESULT	   ; RESULT BUFFER
 23928                                  ;	   DW	   VALUES	   ; VALUE LISTS
 23929                                  ;	   DB	   nid		   ; NUMBER OF KEYWORD/SWITCH SYNONYMS IN FOLLOWING LIST
 23930                                  ;	   DB	   "...",0         ; IF n >0, KEYWORD 1
 23931                                  ;	   :
 23932                                  ;
 23933                                  ;Note:
 23934                                  ;    - The MATCH_FLAG is bit significant. You can set, for example, TIME bit and
 23935                                  ;      DATE bit simalteniously.
 23936                                  ;
 23937                                  ;      The parser examins each bit along with the following priority.
 23938                                  ;
 23939                                  ;      COMPLEX -> DATE -> TIME -> NUMERIC VAL -> SIGNED NUMERIC VAL -> DRIVE ->
 23940                                  ;      FILE SPEC -> SIMPLE STRING.
 23941                                  ;
 23942                                  ;    - When the FUNCTION_FLAG is 0001 or 0002, the STRING pointed to by a pointer
 23943                                  ;      in the result buffer is capitalized.
 23944                                  ;
 23945                                  ;    - Match_Flags 0001H and 0002H have meaning only for the positional.
 23946                                  ;
 23947                                  ;    - The "...",0 (bottom most line) does require '=' or '/'. When you need a
 23948                                  ;      switch, for example, '/A', then STRING points to;
 23949                                  ;
 23950                                  ;			DB    1 	; number of following synonyms
 23951                                  ;			DB   '/A',0
 23952                                  ;
 23953                                  ;      When you need a keyword, for example, 'CODEPAGE=', then "...",0 will be;
 23954                                  ;
 23955                                  ;			DB    1 	; number of following synonyms
 23956                                  ;			DB   'CODEPAGE=',0
 23957                                  ;
 23958                                  ;    - "..." must consist of upper case characters only because the parser
 23959                                  ;      performs pattern matching after converting input to upper case (by
 23960                                  ;      using the current country upper case table)
 23961                                  ;
 23962                                  ;    - One "..." can contain only one switch or keyword. If you need, for
 23963                                  ;      example /A and /B, the format will be;
 23964                                  ;
 23965                                  ;			DB    2 	; number of following synonyms
 23966                                  ;			DB    '/A',0
 23967                                  ;			DB    '/B',0
 23968                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 23969                                  
 23970                                  ;**** Match_Flags
 23971                                  
 23972                                  _$P_Num_Val	   equ	8000h		;AN000; Numeric Value
 23973                                  _$P_SNum_Val	   equ	4000h		;AN000; Signed numeric value
 23974                                  _$P_Simple_S	   equ	2000h		;AN000; Simple string
 23975                                  _$P_Date_S	   equ	1000h		;AN000; Date string
 23976                                  _$P_Time_S	   equ	0800h		;AN000; Time string
 23977                                  _$P_Cmpx_S	   equ	0400h		;AN000; Complex string
 23978                                  _$P_File_Spc	   equ	0200h		;AN000; File Spec
 23979                                  _$P_Drv_Only	   equ	0100h		;AN000; Drive Only
 23980                                  _$P_Qu_String	   equ	0080h		;AN000; Quoted string
 23981                                  _$P_Ig_Colon	   equ	0010h		;AN000; Ignore colon at end in match
 23982                                  _$P_Repeat	   equ	0002h		;AN000; Repeat allowed
 23983                                  _$P_Optional	   equ	0001h		;AN000; Optional
 23984                                  
 23985                                  ;**** Function flags
 23986

 23996 00000004 ????                     .Result_Buf:	 resw 1		; Result buffer address
 23997 00000006 ????                     .Value_List:	 resw 1		;AN000; Value list address
 23998 00000008 ??                       .nid:		 resb 1		;AN000; # of keyword/SW synonyms

 24002                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 24003                                  ; << Value List Definition >>
 24004                                  ;
 24005                                  ;VALUES 	LABEL	BYTE
 24006                                  ;		DB	nval			; NUMBER OF VALUE DEFINITIONS (0 - 3)
 24007                                  ;	     +-
 24008                                  ;	     |	DB	nrng			; NUMBER OF RANGES
 24009                                  ;	     | +DB	ITEM_TAG		; RETURN VALUE IF RANGE MATCHED
 24010                                  ;	     | +DD	X,Y			; RANGE OF VALUES
 24011                                  ;	     |	:
 24012                                  ;	     |	DB	nnval			; NUMBER OF CHOICES
 24013                                  ;	     | +DB	ITEM_TAG		; RETURN VALUE IF NUMBER CHOICE MATCHED
 24014                                  ;	     | +DD	VALUE			; SPECIFIC CHOICE IF NUMBER
 24015                                  ;	     |	:
 24016                                  ;	     |	DB	nstrval 		; NUMBER OF CHOICES
 24017                                  ;	     | +DB	ITEM_TAG		; RETURN VALUE IF STRING CHOICE MATCHED
 24018                                  ;	     | +DW	STRING			; SPECIFIC CHOICE IF STING
 24019                                  ;	     +-	:
 24020                                  ;
 24021                                  ;STRING 	DB	"...",0                 ; ASCIIZ STRING IMAGE
 24022                                  ;
 24023                                  ;Note:
 24024                                  ;    - ITEM_TAG must not be 0FFH, which will be used in the result buffer
 24025                                  ;      when no choice lists are provided.
 24026                                  ;
 24027                                  ;    - STRING must consist of upper case characters only because the parser
 24028                                  ;      performs pattern matching after converting input to upper case (by
 24029                                  ;      using the current country upper case table)

 24038                                  _$P_Len_String	   equ	3		;AN000; Length of a string choice(one DW plus one DB)

 24049                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 24050                                  ; << Result Buffer Definition  >>
 24051                                  ;
 24052                                  ;RESULT 	LABEL	BYTE			; BELOW FILLED IN FOR DEFAULTS
 24053                                  ;		DB	type			; TYPE RETURNED: 0=RESERVED,
 24054                                  ;						;	1=NUMBER, 2=LIST INDEX,
 24055                                  ;						;	3=STRING, 4=COMPLEX,
 24056                                  ;						;	5=FILESPEC, 6=DRIVE
 24057                                  ;						;	7=DATE, 8=TIME
 24058                                  ;						;	9=QUOTED STRING
 24059                                  ;		DB	ITEM_TAG		; MATCHED ITEM TAG
 24060                                  ;
 24061                                  ;		dw	synonym@		; es:@ points to found SYNONYM if provided.
 24062                                  ;
 24063                                  ;            +-
 24064                                  ;	    | DD	n			; VALUE IF NUMBER
 24065                                  ;	    | or
 24066                                  ;	    |	DW	i			; INDEX (OFFSET) INTO VALUE LIST
 24067                                  ;	    |					; (ES presents Segment address)
 24068                                  ;	    | or
 24069                                  ;	    |	DD	STRING			; OFFSET OF STRING VALUE
 24070                                  ;	    | or
 24071                                  ;	    |	DB	drv			; DRIVE NUMBER (1-A, 2-B,..., 26-Z)
 24072                                  ;	    | or
 24073                                  ;	    |	DW	YEAR	   ;(1980-2099)  IN CASE OF DATE
 24074                                  ;	    |	DB	MONTH	   ;(1-12)	 Note: Range check is not performed.
 24075                                  ;	    |	DB	DATE	   ;(1-31)	       0 is filled when the corresponding field was not specified.
 24076                                  ;	    | or
 24077                                  ;	    |	DB	HOUR	   ;(0-23)	  IN CASE OF TIME
 24078                                  ;	    |	DB	MINUTES    ;(0-59)	  Note: Range check is not performed .
 24079                                  ;	    |	DB	SECONDS    ;(0-59)		0 is filled when the corresponding field was not specified .
 24080                                  ;	    |	DB	HUNDREDTHS ;(0-99)
 24081                                  ;	    +-
 24082                                  ;
 24083                                  ;
 24084                                  ;Note: ITEM_TAG is 0FFH when the caller does not specify the choice
 24085                                  ;      list.
 24086                                  ;
 24087                                  ;      YEAR: If the input value for the year is less than 100, parser
 24088                                  ;	     adds 1900 to it.  For example, when 87 is input to parser for
 24089                                  ;	     the year value, he returns 1987.
 24090                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

 24215                                  ;***********************************************************************
 24216                                  ; SysParse;
 24217                                  ;
 24218                                  ;  Function : Parser Entry
 24219                                  ;
 24220                                  ;  Input: DS:SI -> command line
 24221                                  ;	  ES:DI -> parameter block
 24222                                  ;	  cs -> psdata.inc
 24223                                  ;	  CX = operand ordinal
 24224                                  ;
 24225                                  ;	  Note:  ES is the segment containing all the control blocks defined
 24226                                  ;		 by the caller, except for the DOS COMMAND line parms, which
 24227                                  ;		 is in DS.
 24228                                  ;
 24229                                  ;  Output: CY = 1   error of caller, means invalid parameter block or
 24230                                  ;		    invalid value list. But this parser does NOT implement
 24231                                  ;		    this feature. Therefore CY always zero.
 24232                                  ;
 24233                                  ;	   CY = 0   AX = return code
 24234                                  ;		    BL = terminated delimiter code
 24235                                  ;		    CX = new operand ordinal
 24236                                  ;		    SI = set past scaned operand
 24237                                  ;		    DX = selected result buffer
 24238                                  ;
 24239                                  ; Use:	_$P_Skip_Delim, _$P_Chk_EOL, _$P_Chk_Delim, _$P_Chk_DBCS
 24240                                  ;	_$P_Chk_Swtch, _$P_Chk_Pos_Control, _$P_Chk_Key_Control
 24241                                  ;	_$P_Chk_Sw_Control, _$P_Fill_Result
 24242                                  ;
 24243                                  ; Vars: _$P_Ordinal(RW), _$P_RC(RW), _$P_SI_Save(RW), _$P_DX(R), _$P_Terminator(R)
 24244                                  ;	_$P_SaveSI_Cmpx(W), _$P_Flags(RW), _$P_Found_SYNONYM(R), _$P_Save_EOB(W)
 24245                                  ;

 24247                                  ;

 24249                                  ;  4/28/87 : _$P_Val_YH assemble error (tm01)

 24253                                  ;	     DateSW equ 1)	      (tm04)

 24920                                  ; Input:    AH = Item tag

 26458                                  ;**************************************************************************
 26459                                  ; _$P_Chk_DBCS:
 26460                                  ;
 26461                                  ;  Function: Check if a specified byte is in ranges of the DBCS lead bytes
 26462                                  ;
 26463                                  ;  Input:
 26464                                  ;	  AL	= Code to be examineed
 26465                                  ;
 26466                                  ;  Output:
 26467                                  ;	  If CF is on then a lead byte of DBCS
 26468                                  ;
 26469                                  ; Use: INT 21h w/AH=63

 26471                                  ; Vars:  _$P_DBCSEV_Seg(RW), _$P_DBCSEV_Off(RW)

 26475 00001CB4 1E                      	push	ds			;AN000;

 26489 00001CC5 55                      	push	bp			;AN000;

 26498 00001CD0 09DB                    	or	bx,bx			;AN000; (tm11)
 26499 00001CD2 07                      	pop	es			;AN000;
 26500 00001CD3 5D                      	pop	bp			;AN000;
 26501 00001CD4 5F                      	pop	di			;AN000;

 27108                                  ;   Module:   HIGHVAR.INC - Data common to LOADHIGH and DEVICEHIGH, res seg
 27109                                  ;
 27110                                  ;   Date:     May 14, 1992
 27111                                  ;
 27112                                  ;******************************************************************************
 27113                                  ;
 27114                                  ;   Modification log:
 27115                                  ;
 27116                                  ;     DATE    WHO      DESCRIPTION
 27117                                  ;   --------  -------  --------------------------------------------------------
 27118                                  ;   05/14/92  t-richj  Original
 27119                                  ;   06/21/92  t-richj  Final revisions before check-in
 27120                                  ;
 27121                                  ;******************************************************************************
 27122                                  ;
 27123                                  ; There are two primary definitions which need to be made, selectively, before
 27124                                  ; this include file should be used.  These are:
 27125                                  ;    HV_Extern - If this has been defined, variables for this module will be
 27126                                  ;                declared as external.  Otherwise, variables will be declared
 27127                                  ;                public, as well as defined, here.  LoadHigh declares HV_Extern
 27128                                  ;                in stub.asm and loadhi.asm, and does not declare it in
 27129                                  ;                rdata.asm... DeviceHigh does not declare HV_Extern anywhere
 27130                                  ;                (as only one module, sysconf.asm, includes this file).
 27131                                  ;    HV_LoadHigh - This should be defined when this module is going into
 27132                                  ;                  command.com, for LoadHigh.  All of loadhi.asm, stub.asm and
 27133                                  ;                  rdata.asm define this, while io.sys' sysconf.asm does not.
 27134                                  ;
 27135                                  ;******************************************************************************
 27136                                  
 27137                                  ; To keep track of which UMBs were specified on the DH/LH command lines, and
 27138                                  ; to keep track of the minimum sizes given for each, there're two arrays kept
 27139                                  ; in { IO.SYS: sysinitseg / COMMAND.COM: DATARES }... each is MAXUMB elements
 27140                                  ; big.  16 should be around 14 too many for most users, so there's no expected
 27141                                  ; space problem (it's just such a nice round number, eh?).
 27142                                  
 27143                                  MAXUMB	equ	16
 27144                                  
 27145                                  ; Memory elements owned by the system are marked as PSP address 8 in both the
 27146                                  ; USA and Japan; Japanese systems also use 9 under more bizzarre conditions.
 27147                                  
 27148                                  FreePSPOwner	equ	0	; Free MCBs all have an owner PSP address of 0
 27149                                  SystemPSPOwner	equ	8
 27150                                  ;JapanPSPOwner	equ	9
 27151                                  
 27152                                  ; for LoadHigh and DeviceHigh:
 27153                                  ;
 27154                                  ;	fInHigh - Is set to 1 during HideUMBs(), and back to zero in
 27155                                  ;	          UnHideUMBs().
 27156                                  ;	fUmbTiny - Is set to 1 if the user has specified /S on the command-
 27157                                  ;	           line.
 27158                                  ;	SegLoad - Segment address for first UMB specified; set automatically.
 27159                                  ;	UmbLoad - The load UMB number; for example, this is 3 if the user has
 27160                                  ;	          given a command-line like "/L:3,500;4"
 27161                                  ;	UmbUsed - An array of characters, each of which is 1 iff the UMB
 27162                                  ;	          matching its index number was specified on the command-line;
 27163                                  ;	          for example, after "/L:3,500;4;7", UmbUsed[3], [4] and [7]
 27164                                  ;	          will be set to 1. All others will be set to 0.
 27165                                  ;	UmbSize - An array of words, each of which is interpereted as a size
 27166                                  ;	          specified by the user for a UMB (in the above example, all
 27167                                  ;	          elements would be zero save UmbSize[3], which would be 500.
 27168                                  ;	fm_umb - Set to the old UMB link-state (0x80 or 0x00)
 27169                                  ;	fm_strat - Set to the old memory-allocation strategy (0$00000???)
 27170                                  ;	fm_argc  - Number of arguments received by ParseVar() (see ParseVar()
 27171                                  ;	           for details).
 27172                                  
 27173 00001F00 00                      fInHigh:  db	0
 27174 00001F01 00                      fUmbTiny: db	0
 27175 00001F02 0000                    SegLoad:  dw	0
 27176 00001F04 00                      UmbLoad:  db	0
 27177 00001F05 00<rep 10h>             UmbUsed:  times MAXUMB db 0 ; times 16 db 0  ; db 16 dup(?)
 27178 00001F15 0000<rep 10h>           UmbSize:  times MAXUMB dw 0 ; times 16 dw 0  ; dw 16 dup(?)
 27179 00001F35 00                      fm_umb:   db	0
 27180 00001F36 00                      fm_strat: db	0
 27181 00001F37 00                      fm_argc:  db	0	
 27182                                  
 27183                                  ; UmbLoad is set to UNSPECIFED, below, until /L:umb is read; at which point
 27184                                  ; UmbLoad is set to the UMB number given.
 27185                                  
 27186                                  UNSPECIFIED	equ	-1
 27187                                  
 27188                                  ;%endif ; 27/10/2022
